article.content: Hackers have launched more than 240,000 exploit attempts against a WordPress core race-condition flaw that exposes websites to unauthenticated remote code execution during upgrades. Wordfence researcher István Márton reported that probing began October 28, 2026, the day WordPress released security patches. Tracked as CVE-2026-119977, the upgrade-window remote code execution issue affects unpatched releases across branches 4.7 through 7.1.3 and carries a CVSS score of 8.1. Hackers Launch Over 240,000 Attacks The exploitation primitive involves predictable, web-accessible staging directories created during full-package core upgrades. Attackers send HTTP requests to installer scripts such as /wp-content/upgrade/wordpress-6.9.11/setup-config.php, attempting to reach extracted installation files before cleanup. If successful, they can complete the staged installation, create an administrator account, and upload malicious PHP. This provides a foothold for server-side execution, persistent backdoors, content manipulation, and sensitive-data exfiltration without credentials or an authenticated session on the targeted production website. Unlike campaigns using malicious PHP plugins through hijacked administrator sessions, this attack targets standalone installer files during a temporary filesystem exposure. Wordfence Firewall (Sourcee: Wordfence) Exploitation requires the staging directory to exist, permit external access, and remain available long enough to complete the installation sequence. The CVE record classifies the defect as CWE-367, a time-of-check time-of-use race condition. These timing requirements explain its high attack complexity despite potentially severe confidentiality, integrity, and availability impacts. Wordfence observed the heaviest probing between October 29 and November 1, with more than 74,000 attempts blocked on October 30 alone. Leading sources included103.59.160.171, responsible for over 74,900 requests; 2001:df1:e8c0::106b, exceeding 40,400; and 51.89.103.78, exceeding 34,600. These figures represent blocked requests, not confirmed compromised websites. Automated scanners repeatedly requesting predictable staging paths must still hit the narrow upgrade window and finish exploitation before temporary files disappear, making successful compromise substantially harder than generating traffic. Administrators should inspect access logs for external requests to PHP files beneath /wp-content/upgrade/, particularly setup-config.php. Legitimate upgrades do not require such requests. Investigations should also examine leftover staging directories, unexpected plugins, unauthorized administrator accounts, and altered PHP files. Separately observed administrator-account backdoors illustrate why account and plugin inventories matter during incident response, although those campaigns are not evidence of exploitation here. Missing suspicious log entries alone cannot establish that a site remains uncompromised. WordPress recommends immediately installing version 7.1.4 or the corresponding patched branch release. Updating an affected installation still invokes its vulnerable upgrade process once, so administrators can first block web access to PHP files under /wp-content/upgrade/. Wordfence requires an optimized firewall running in Extended Protection mode because staged scripts do not load WordPress. Premium protection arrived October 28; free users receive the rule November 27. Patching removes the underlying exposure from subsequent upgrades. generated.caption:
Over 240,000 attacks targeting WordPress could let hackers take over websites! During updates, a temporary folder is briefly exposed. Attackers exploit this window to install malicious files and create admin accounts, gaining full control of unpatched sites. Update your WordPress to version 7.1.4 or newer immediately to stay safe.

Save and share this post! Follow @CyberShieldAlerts for daily updates.
generated.script: Critical alert for WordPress site owners! Hackers have launched over 240,000 attacks exploiting a severe core vulnerability. This flaw, affecting WordPress versions 4.7 through 7.1.3, allows unauthenticated remote code execution during upgrades. Attackers can create admin accounts and upload malicious code, giving them full control without your login. They're targeting temporary files created during updates. This means your website is exposed to server-side execution and data theft. Don't wait. Immediately update your WordPress installation to version 7.1.4 or its corresponding patched release. For extra security, temporarily block web access to PHP files under /wp-content/upgrade/ before updating.

slides.headlineRest: Launched Against WordPress Core RCE Flaw
slides.body: Hackers have initiated over 240,000 exploit attempts targeting a race-condition flaw within WordPress core. This vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-119977, allows unauthenticated remote code execution during website upgrades. Successful exploitation can lead to administrative account creation, malicious PHP uploads, and server-side execution. WordPress strongly advises users to immediately install version 7.1.4 or the latest patched branch release. For an additional layer of protection during the update process, administrators can temporarily block web access to PHP files under /wp-content/upgrade/.
slides.hindiSummary: हैकर्स ने वर्डप्रेस कोर में एक रिमोट कोड निष्पादन त्रुटि का फायदा उठाने के लिए 240,000 से अधिक हमले किए हैं, इसलिए तुरंत अपडेट करें।
